name: Funding crowding filter on trend-vol-target (BTC, ETH daily)

sections.hypothesis: Trend-vol-target (the only strategy marked Pursue) does better if it also stands aside while perpetual funding is crowded (7-day average 30% a year or more): crowded longs late in a trend are when trends reverse hardest.
sections.rationale: Perpetual futures funding is paid between longs and shorts every 8 hours to keep the perp near spot. High funding means the market is full of leveraged longs paying to stay in; a fall can then cascade through forced liquidations. That is information about positioning that isn't in the spot price chart, and every price-only idea in the trial log has failed or turned out to be trend following. Kestrel only reads the data (Binance's public archive, every 8h since 2020-01); it never trades perpetuals, so Australia's limits on retail perps don't apply. Weak points: funding rises in strong bull markets, so stepping aside when it is high may mean missing the best runs (the same way Fear & Greed contrarian sold the start of 2020 and 2024's rallies); funding was much wilder in 2020-21 than since, so the signal may fire mostly in one regime; and the threshold is a judgement. Disclosure: before writing this note I looked at the funding distribution itself (7-day annualised average at or above 30% on 11% of days for BTC and 13.5% for ETH, 2020-25), but not at any returns conditioned on it. As an add-on: trend following is already out in falling markets, so a funding filter can only help by cutting exposure late in rising ones, before the trend rule notices a reversal.
sections.rules: Daily bars. funding_7d = the average of the coin's own perpetual funding settlements in the 7 days up to the bar's close, each rate annualised (rate per interval x settlements per year), each settlement known from its settlement time; unknown (null) when the window starts before the history or the newest settlement is more than 1 day old. Crowded = funding_7d at or above 30% a year, about 3x Binance's default rate of 0.01% per 8h (about 11% a year): a round multiple of the exchange's neutral level, not fitted to returns. An unknown reading leaves the base position unchanged. Decide at the close, trade at the next open; 2% no-trade band; long only, spot; 10 bps fee, 1 bp half-spread, square-root impact. Base position: trend-vol-target with its default settings (20/60/120-day trend votes, 30-day volatility, 50% volatility target). Target weight 0 while crowded, otherwise trend-vol-target's own weight.
sections.falsification: BTCUSDT 1d and ETHUSDT 1d, 2020-01 to 2025-10, default parameters, 330 USDT, run once each. Comparison: trend-vol-target with its defaults on the same coin, window, cash and config, run once each now (the earlier runs used an older costs config) and logged as trials of its own note. Reject unless, on both markets: (1) Sharpe is above trend-vol-target's; (2) max drawdown is no worse than trend-vol-target's; (3) total return is at least 90% of trend-vol-target's (a filter that only cuts exposure must not buy its Sharpe by giving up most of the return); (4) break-even cost is at least twice the cost paid. A pass goes to walk-forward before any change to the Pursue decision.
sections.parameters: crowded_pct 30; trend-vol-target at its defaults. Only these are pre-registered; any other threshold or trend setting is a new trial.
sections.costs: Trend-vol-target already rebalances often (volatility sizing); the filter adds a full exit and re-entry each time funding crosses the threshold during an uptrend, at about 22 bps a round trip.

history.reason: Pre-registered test (BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT 1d, 2020-01..2025-10, crowded_pct 30; runs 20261113-073755-8fc78a and 20261113-073757-8f513d, against trend-vol-target re-run on the current config: 20261113-073755-da13da and 20261113-073757-155a79). BTC failed rule 3: Sharpe 1.27 vs 1.21 and drawdown -44.9% vs -48.3% (both better), but +537% vs +639%, 84% of trend-vol-target's return against 90% required. ETH failed rules 1-3: Sharpe 1.09 vs 1.23, drawdown -38.5% vs -38.4%, +455% vs +871%. The filter cut exposure (44% vs 50% on BTC, 34% vs 41% on ETH) more than it cut risk. Trend-vol-target stays as it was.
